meta.subtitle: Power and thermal infrastructure for AI data centers: a backlog that more than doubled and net cash, against a forward multiple that has to hold.

advisories: model vs Street expected return diverge by 76pp — informational, not scored

analystSentiment.commentary: The Street is positive but not unanimous. Of 28 analysts, 24 rate the shares Buy, 4 Hold and 0 Sell, a consensus of Strong Buy. The consensus price target is $338.15, {+ +33.4% +} above the $253.51 quote, with a median of $345.00 and a range of $236.00 to $427.00; every target except the lowest sits above the current price. The consensus target lands close to what today's forward multiple would give on the FY27E consensus EPS, so the Street is in effect assuming that the multiple holds for another year while earnings grow into it. That is the point where we differ. Our Base lets the multiple ease as growth slows, and our Bear prices a pause in data-center spending, so our fair value sits well below the consensus target (see valuation).

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Vertiv Holdings Co designs, manufactures and services critical digital infrastructure: the power, thermal and rack systems that keep data centers, communication networks and commercial and industrial facilities running. The portfolio spans AC and DC power management, low/medium voltage switchgear and busbar, air cooled and liquid cooled thermal management, racks, single phase UPS, integrated modular solutions and energy storage, sold under brands including Vertiv, Liebert, NetSure, Geist and Avocent. Lifecycle services cover preventative maintenance, remote monitoring, fluid management and spare parts. The company is headquartered in Westerville, Ohio, does business in more than 130 countries and carries a market capitalization of about $97.6B. In its second-quarter 10-Q, management describes very robust growth in demand for data centers supporting artificial intelligence and high-performance compute, and says it is investing in global capacity to meet current and anticipated demand.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body: Vertiv's order book and guidance point to another year of fast growth. Backlog more than doubled during 2025, management raised its 2026 guidance across all key metrics in July, margins are widening, and the company reached a net-cash position at the end of the second quarter. The question is price. The shares trade on a premium forward multiple, and the Street's targets need that multiple to hold a year out. Our Base lets it ease as growth slows, and our Bear prices a pause in data-center spending. On those scenarios the expected return is positive but small next to the Bear downside, so the derived label is HOLD. It is a close call, and the valuation section sets out what would tip it.

catalysts: Third-quarter results: guidance calls for organic growth well above the second quarter's pace, and delivery would support the FY27E consensus (see growth).
Backlog conversion: most of the year-end 2025 backlog was expected to ship within about the next year and a half, which supports revenue into 2027.
Margin: third-quarter guidance implies a wider adjusted operating margin than the second quarter's.
Tariff refunds: Vertiv has begun filing IEEPA refund claims, though it says the amount, timing and likelihood of any recovery are uncertain.
risks: AI and data-center capex: demand rests on customers' spending, and a pause is our Bear case.
Large-customer terms: big cloud and colocation buyers can press on price, contract terms and delivery penalties.
Order timing: lumpy orders and deferrable backlog can move results from quarter to quarter.
Valuation: a premium multiple can compress well before estimates change.
Trade and geopolitics: tariffs, conflict and supply-chain congestion affect costs and delivery timing.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary: Revenue grew from $5.0B in FY21 to $10.2B in FY25, and growth picked up to {+ +27.7% +} in FY25 from {+ +16.7% +} in FY24. Profitability rose faster: gross margin moved from 30.5% to 36.3% and operating margin from 5.2% to 17.9% over FY21–FY25, and diluted EPS went from $0.33 to $3.41, after a $0.04 loss per share in FY22. In the second quarter of 2026, net sales of $3,274.3 million rose {+ 24.1% +} year over year. The company splits that into 18% organic growth, 5% from acquisitions and 1% from currency, and says minor timing shifts from temporary supply chain congestion and multi-phased project execution held sales back. Gross margin was 37.7% against 34.0% a year earlier, which the MD&A attributes primarily to the mix of product and service sales, and GAAP operating margin was 19.5%. GAAP operating profit also absorbed higher amortization of intangibles, $73.7 million against $46.9 million a year earlier. Adjusted figures run higher. Adjusted operating margin was 22.6%, {+ up 410 basis points +}, which the company credits to operational execution, continued strong productivity and favorable price-cost, inclusive of tariff impacts and countermeasures. Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.52, {+ up 60% +}, against GAAP diluted EPS of $1.27, {+ up 53% +}. Trailing-twelve-month margins are 38.0% gross, 18.9% operating and 15.1% net.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary: Net debt fell from $2.5B in FY21 to $1.2B in FY25 while total debt held at $2.9B from FY23 onward, so the improvement came from cash and short-term investments, which reached $1.7B. Total equity rose from $1.4B to $3.9B over the same years. The company reported a net cash position at the end of the second quarter of 2026, with $5.6 billion of liquidity. The trailing-twelve-month row instead shows net debt at 0.1x EBITDA; the two may use different dates or definitions, and we take the company's quarter-end statement as the current position. Interest coverage is 41.4x. The current ratio is 1.38 on a trailing basis against 1.55 at the end of FY25, lower but backed by a net-cash position. Debt does not constrain the investment plan. The balance-sheet risk we see is the fixed cost of capacity built ahead of demand, which would weigh on margins if orders slowed.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary: Operating cash flow rose from $0.2B in FY21 to $2.1B in FY25, and free cash flow reached $1.9B in FY25, an 18.4% FCF margin, after a negative FY22. Capital spending is now stepping up: the MD&A says second-quarter capital investment was significantly higher than a year earlier, and the company expects full-year 2026 capital expenditure of approximately 4.0% of revenue, at the high end of its range. In the second quarter, operating cash flow was $1,100 million and adjusted free cash flow $925 million, {+ up 241% +} and {+ up 234% +} respectively. The company credits higher adjusted operating profit, working capital efficiency and lower cash interest, partially offset by higher cash taxes and capital expenditure; a quarter helped by working capital should not be annualized. Full-year 2026 adjusted free cash flow is guided at $2,400–$2,600 million. That is a non-GAAP measure, so it is not directly comparable with the FY25 free cash flow above. Shareholder returns are small: FY25 had no buybacks after $0.6B in FY24, and the dividend yields 0.10%. The trailing FCF yield of 3.0% shows how much of the share price rests on future growth rather than current cash.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: On the vendor's figures, Vertiv trades at 57.4x trailing earnings, 8.5x sales and 38.1x trailing EV/EBITDA. The forward (NTM) P/E of 37.6x sits close to the price over the FY26E consensus EPS of $6.73, so we treat it as today's current-year multiple. The ~27.8x on FY27E consensus EPS of $9.12 is today's price over earnings two years out; it is not the comparison for a value set a year from now. Our scenarios value the shares a year out, so the like-for-like reference for their multiples is that current-year multiple. Consensus FY26E EPS sits inside the company's adjusted EPS guidance rather than its GAAP guidance (see growth), so the forward multiples are on an adjusted basis. Peer multiples are pending a peer data source, and the page carries no history of Vertiv's own multiple, so each scenario multiple is our assumption with its basis stated. The shares trade at $253.51, well below the 52-week high of $379.94 and above the low of $133.85, even though guidance was raised in July. No captured source explains the decline. It shows both that the market paid much more for this story within the past year and that it has been willing to pay much less.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Demand stays robust, the backlog converts on schedule, further guidance raises follow, and the FY27E consensus EPS is met or beaten. A year out the shares regain their 52-week high, a price the market paid within the past year; on FY27E consensus EPS that is a premium to today's current-year multiple, which a still-growing order book and a third-quarter acceleration could support.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Vertiv lands its raised 2026 guidance and the FY27E consensus EPS is met, but a year out the shares trade at 33x those earnings, our assumption: a few turns below today's current-year multiple, because consensus EPS growth from FY26E to FY27E is slower than the 58–61% adjusted EPS growth guided for 2026. Holding today's multiple instead would put the Base close to the Street's consensus target.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: AI data-center spending pauses or a large customer defers orders, so FY27 EPS stalls at the FY26E consensus instead of rising. The shares de-rate to 25x those earnings, our assumption for earnings that have paused rather than fallen, set well below today's current-year multiple. It is not a floor: the shares traded lower than this within the past year.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: Weighting Bull, Base and Bear at 25%, 55% and 20% gives a fair value of $294.15, an expected upside of {+ +16.0% +} against a bear-case downside of {- -33.7% -}, a reward/risk of 0.48×. That clears the +10.0% bar for a BUY but not the 0.50× reward/risk bar, so the derived label is HOLD. The weights rest on the order book, not on the multiples. Base carries the most weight because the July guidance raise and a mostly firm backlog make delivery of the FY27E consensus the likeliest path. Bull's weight reflects a third-quarter guide that points to faster organic growth, held back because the case also needs the multiple to rise from today's level after a year in which it fell. Bear sits just below Bull. A full stall in FY27 earnings within a year would need customers to defer or cancel firm orders, which usually carries penalties; we do not weight it lower, because the risk factors name exactly that mechanism and the shares have already fallen well below their high without an explained cause. The call is close, and it is HOLD by a narrow margin. Moving five points of weight from Bear to Bull, a Bear multiple one turn higher, or a Base multiple one turn richer would each derive BUY. The deciding judgment is whether the multiple holds a year out. We think it eases as growth slows; a reader who expects it to hold would rate the shares BUY. The target range of $275 to $325 brackets the Base.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Our data carries Vertiv as one consolidated line with no regional or product split. The 10-Q MD&A, however, refers to segment results by region (the Americas, Asia Pacific, and Europe, Middle East & Africa) and by offering; the captured excerpt ends before that section, so this report discusses the business on a consolidated basis. By offering, the portfolio combines power management, thermal management, racks and integrated modular systems with lifecycle services. In the second quarter, Product sales increased $487.5 million and Services & Spares sales increased $148.7 million year over year, so both grew and products drove most of the dollar gain. The value of the combination is that Vertiv can sell power and cooling together as rack density rises, and then service the installed equipment.

moatFactors.name: Installed base and services
moatFactors.body: Lifecycle services such as preventative maintenance, remote monitoring, fluid management and spare parts attach to equipment already in the field, and Services & Spares grew in the second quarter (see segments). Recurring service work on uptime-critical equipment likely raises the cost of switching suppliers, though the page shows neither services margins nor retention.

moatFactors.name: Systems-level breadth
moatFactors.body: The MD&A says customer requirements are moving toward higher-density environments, including hybrid air and liquid cooling and high voltage direct current power, and that customers increasingly prioritize speed of deployment and execution certainty. A supplier of power, thermal, racks and prefabricated modular systems fits that shift. The sources do not show how often customers buy the full system.

moatFactors.name: Qualification cycles
moatFactors.body: The 10-K describes a lengthy contracting, design and qualification process for large deployments and new products. That favors suppliers that are already qualified, although the same risk factor says it makes orders less predictable.

moatFactors.name: Customer power and competition
moatFactors.body: Large communication network, cloud/hyperscale, neocloud and colocation providers comprise a material portion of the customer base and often require more favorable terms. The company also lists competition in its industry among its risks. The page names no competitor and gives no market-share data, so we cannot measure Vertiv's position against rivals.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat narrow. Qualification cycles and an installed base that needs servicing give incumbents real protection, and the FY23–FY25 margin step-up (see financials) shows that Vertiv could price well in a tight market. Two forces cap it. Large customers hold bargaining power over terms and penalties, and demand rides a data-center spending cycle that Vertiv does not control. The data show no period of slower demand in which to test whether the margin gains hold, so we do not treat them as proof of a wide moat.

points: Per the 2025 Form 10-K, Vertiv's estimated combined order backlog was approximately $15.0 billion at December 31, 2025, against approximately $7.2 billion a year earlier, and the majority was considered firm and expected to be delivered within 12 to 18 months. Acquisitions added to pipeline and backlog, and their contracts may let customers reduce firm orders or terminate. The figure dates from the end of 2025, and the captured 10-Q excerpt gives no update.

In July management raised full-year 2026 guidance to net sales of $13,800–$14,200 million, organic growth of 30–32% and adjusted diluted EPS of $6.65–$6.75, against GAAP diluted EPS guidance of $5.82–$5.92. Consensus for FY26E, ~$14B of revenue (+37%), sits at the midpoint of the sales range, and consensus EPS sits inside the adjusted range.

Third-quarter guidance calls for net sales of $3,650–$3,850 million and organic growth of 34–36%, well above the second quarter's organic pace. The company describes the second quarter's shortfall as minor timing shifts, so the third quarter will test that explanation.

Adjusted operating margin is guided at 23.3–24.3% for 2026 and 24.0–25.0% for the third quarter, with full-year adjusted operating profit of $3,285–$3,365 million. The company frames the gains as coming from execution, productivity and price-cost.

Consensus expects revenue to keep rising in FY27, to $18.2B, though at a slower rate than in FY26. The MD&A says Vertiv anticipates further investment in global capacity, and that it is investing in prefabricated, modular and factory-integrated solutions as customers prioritize speed of deployment.

management.leadership: Per the proxy statement dated April 24, 2026, Giordano Albertazzi is Chief Executive Officer and Dave Cote serves as Executive Chairman; the company currently separates the two roles. Craig Chamberlin became Chief Financial Officer on November 10, 2025, and the proxy lists the former Chief Financial Officer, David Fallon, as a 2025 named executive officer as well. The other named executives are Anand Sanghi (President, Americas), Stephanie Gill (Chief Legal Officer) and Scott Armul (Chief Product & Technology Officer). The proxy credits Mr. Albertazzi's leadership with improvements in operational execution and with what it calls historic financial results in 2025, and the second-quarter results (see financials) are consistent with that record. The finance chief changed less than a year ago, which we treat as a modest continuity point rather than a concern.
management.capitalAllocation: The record points to reinvestment first. FY25 had no buybacks (see cash flow) and the dividend is small, while capital spending is rising and the proxy names three 2025 acquisitions: Waylay (generative AI software for predictive analytics), Great Lakes (data rack enclosures and integrated infrastructure) and PurgeRite (fluid management services for liquid cooling). Acquisitions contributed to second-quarter sales growth (see financials). The company says its net-cash position provides significant strategic optionality, and the MD&A says it anticipates further investment in global capacity. That allocation suits a business with this order book. The cost is a larger fixed base, which would make a Bear-case slowdown more painful for margins.
management.governance: Per the April 24, 2026 proxy, the Board has determined that nine director nominees are independent under SEC and NYSE rules; the excerpt does not give the total board size. The chairman and CEO roles are separate, but the chairman is an executive: Mr. Cote, as Executive Chairman, acts as the primary liaison between senior management and the independent directors, and the company has no policy on whether the roles should be separate or combined. Related-person transactions above $120,000 are reviewed by the Audit Committee members who are not interested in the transaction, under a written policy that also pre-approves certain transaction types; the excerpt describes no specific transactions. Pay leans on performance. The CEO's opportunity consists primarily of stock options and a performance bonus. The 2022 strategic performance awards cliff-vest in January 2027 after 220% of the final tranche was earned, and a similar EPS-based program starts in 2026. For outside holders, pay is tied to the share price and EPS, and the January 2027 cliff vest supports management retention until then. The main limit on the board's independent oversight is that an executive, not an independent director, chairs it.

idiosyncratic: AI and data-center dependence: the 10-K says a substantial portion of the business depends on continued growth in customers' data-center and communication infrastructure, and names shifts in the level or focus of AI spending, capacity built in excess of demand and delays in permits as reasons demand could fall. This is the mechanism behind our Bear case (see valuation). Because backlog cancellations usually carry penalties, a slowdown would likely show first in new orders and in the multiple rather than in reported revenue.

Large-customer leverage: per the 10-K, large customers often require more favorable terms, including on large multi-year AI projects, and may impose substantial penalties for product or service failures or late delivery. As project scale and urgency rise, they may also seek more stringent delivery commitments, which raises the cost of any execution slip during the capacity build-out.

Order timing and backlog: long sales cycles and customers' right to reduce or defer firm orders, usually with penalties, can make revenue swing between quarters; the second quarter's timing shifts (see financials) are an example. Contracts from acquired businesses may have differing terms that let customers reduce firm orders or terminate.

Executing the capacity build: Vertiv is expanding capacity for current and anticipated demand, and the MD&A refers to inherent complexities and challenges associated with very robust market growth. The 10-Q's list of forward-looking risks also includes failure to remediate material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting; the captured excerpt does not describe them, so we cannot judge their scope.
risks.systemic: Vertiv's demand rides one cycle: data-center capital spending. The 10-K names the ways that cycle could slow, among them changes in the economy, shifts in AI spending, capacity built in excess of demand, permit delays, and local zoning decisions, community opposition or moratoria that limit data-center construction. The 10-Q adds a trade and geopolitical layer. U.S. tariffs, foreign retaliatory measures, the US-Israel and Iran war and wider foreign-policy developments have affected, and are likely to continue to affect, supply chains, input, fuel and transportation costs, customer demand and exchange rates. The company manages these through supply chain diversification, regional sourcing, pricing actions and hedging. The February 2026 Supreme Court decision invalidating IEEPA tariffs could return some tariff costs, but Vertiv says the amount, timing and likelihood of any refund are uncertain. With net cash, higher interest rates would hurt Vertiv mainly through its customers' cost of building data centers rather than through its own debt. Because the shares carry a premium multiple, a broad shock would likely reach the valuation before the reported results.

body: We rate Vertiv HOLD with a target range of $275 to $325. The business case is strong: an order book that more than doubled in 2025, guidance raised in July, widening margins and a net-cash balance sheet. The issue is what the market will pay a year from now. Our expected upside of {+ +16.0% +} clears the BUY bar, but the reward/risk of 0.48× does not, because a pause in data-center spending at a lower multiple would take the shares well below today's price.

The label is close to BUY and rests on our judgment that the multiple eases as growth slows. On these scenarios, BUY would derive at a price just below $253.51, or if third-quarter results came in line with guidance and lifted the FY27E consensus enough to raise the Base. SELL would derive if the price rose a little above our Base value of $301 with the outlook unchanged, or if orders weakened enough to make the Bear the central case.
